patch.value: Bidirectional interop adapters: import from and export to external trackers as packages, preserving provenance and round-trip fidelity

Adoption of a repository-native tracker is gated on the work already living somewhere else, and the exit story matters as much as the entry story: a tool that cannot export its data is a tool teams refuse to adopt. Today there are one-directional importers for two adjacent formats and a CSV export, which is enough to demonstrate the extension surface but not enough to move a real project in or out. This feature defines an interop adapter contract - a declared mapping between an external tracker's item model and the pm schema, provenance stamped on every imported item, idempotent re-import that updates rather than duplicates, and an export that a fresh workspace can re-import to an equivalent state - and delivers it as packages rather than core surface, so each adapter can evolve at the external system's pace without touching the CLI.

An interop adapter contract is published in the SDK: schema mapping declaration, provenance stamping, idempotency key derivation, and conflict policy for re-import; Imported items carry the external system, its identifier, and the import run as provenance, so a re-import updates the same items rather than creating duplicates; A round-trip acceptance test exports a non-trivial workspace, imports it into a fresh workspace, and asserts equivalence of items, relationships, and evidence links within declared lossy-field limits; History and relationships survive import where the source provides them, and where it does not the gap is declared in the adapter's capability manifest rather than silently dropped; At least one adapter beyond the existing formats ships as a package against the contract, proving the contract on a system pm does not control
Work can enter and leave pm without losing its provenance
A universal project management substrate that cannot ingest existing work or hand it back is a substrate nobody can adopt with existing projects, which is nearly all of them.
Removes the largest practical adoption barrier, makes the exit story explicit rather than implied, and demonstrates the package platform on integrations the project does not own.
A published adapter contract with provenance and idempotency, a proven round trip, and at least one third-system adapter shipped as a package.
The package platform, typed relationship persistence, and bulk transaction primitives all shipped, so an adapter can now be written entirely against public SDK surface.
